mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% indicates a tightening labor market that boosts corporate hiring and profit growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE falls below 3.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer spending and economic expansion, which drives positive equity returns as corporate earnings rise; the effect is multiplicative and not additive.
failure_condition: The joint effect of HOUST and RSAFS growth is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in predicting 5-day returns, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening manufacturing activity and potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as investors price in recession risks.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC for INDPRO in this regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly growth in real GDP (GDPC1) above the 2% trend rate indicates sustained economic expansion, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of quarters when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2%, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI increase above 2.5% signals persistent inflation that triggers central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as bond yields rise and equity valuations contract.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL monthly change exceeds 2.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days; the effect is multiplicative and not additive.
failure_condition: The joint effect of PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in predicting 20-day returns, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% signals reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as equity valuations adjust downward.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of monetary tightening cycles when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5%, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS in this regime is below 0.03.
